answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. Consequently, an attacker with a large flock pays more to keep it alive than it can ever extract, which is why Sybil campaigns fail here.. The design works because cost compounds over compute, time, and reputation, growing faster than the influence the cluster can extract. Consider a ivory as the anchor of the cost.
